reference_diagnosis.name: Episodic ataxia type 1 (KCNA1)
reference_diagnosis.basis: Brief, frequent kinesigenic/startle-triggered ataxic attacks with interictal myokymia; EMG myokymic discharges; KCNA1 variant.

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Brief attacks triggered by sudden movement
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: PKD attacks are dystonic/choreic, not ataxic with dysarthria; no myokymia
Attacks last hours; interictal nystagmus; not provoked by sudden movement
Fully responsive throughout, consistent movement trigger, normal EEG and MRI; interictal myokymia is not explained

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Attacks with emotional upset in a teenager
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Stereotyped kinesigenic trigger reproduced in clinic, interictal myokymia, and a father with the same history

key_evidence_gaps.question: Response to carbamazepine or acetazolamide
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Both may help EA1; PKD responds very well to low-dose carbamazepine

held_out_evidence.result: Heterozygous pathogenic KCNA1 variant; PRRT2 negative.

discriminating_investigations.investigation: Careful phenomenology of a provoked attack

cant_miss.why_required: Treatable: carbamazepine or acetazolamide may help
Treatable with low-dose carbamazepine; the paediatrician raised it
cant_miss.status_in_record: open but less likely: provoked attack is ataxic, not dystonic or choreic
partly addressed: interictal EEG normal and awareness preserved; no attack recorded

cant_miss.condition: Metabolic paroxysmal disorder (calcium, magnesium, glucose, thyroid)

red_flags_for_wrong_reasoning: Accepting PKD solely because attacks are movement-triggered
Stating any diagnosis as established rather than as a hypothesis for physician review
Recommending treatment as an instruction rather than a consideration for the treating physician
Citing literature that does not exist or does not support the specific claim
Asserting case facts that are not in the case record
Treating the brief post-attack hand stiffness as dystonia that proves PKD
clinician_review_notes: Clinical review 2026-10-17 (pending Wiki sign-off). Well built EA1 case with a clear discriminating attack in clinic. Added epilepsy and functional hypotheses, cant_miss, one red flag and expected behaviour.
expected_system_behavior: EA1 should rank first. The system should describe the provoked attack as ataxic rather than dystonic, highlight interictal myokymia, separate EA1 from PKD and EA2, and suggest EMG and KCNA1/PRRT2 genetics. The father's similar spells support autosomal dominant inheritance.
